Did u know where and for what people already use stablecoins like real money❓

People are already use stablecoins like real money in many places and situations, especially where banking is weak, fees are high or currencies are unstable

🌍 Everyday Use Cases are next:
Sending money abroad
In countries like Mexico, Philippines, Nigeria people use stablecoins to send money across borders because its cheaper and faster than Western Union or banks

Savings in unstable economies
In places like Venezuela, Argentina, Turkey, people store money in USDT/USDC instead of their local currency to escape high inflation

Payments for goods,services
In parts of Africa and Southeast Asia, freelancers and small businesses get paid in stablecoins because it avoids high banking fees and delays

Crypto trading and DeFi
Its the most common way, when traders worldwide use stablecoins as digital dollars to move in and out of crypto quickly

Merchant payments
Some stores, online shops and even street vendors in places like Nigeria, Brazil, and Lebanon accept stablecoins directly as payment

Buying real estate
In Dubai you can do that without any problems, check the process below👇

and how @PlasmaFDN  can improve these procceses?

Rn, stablecoins are super useful  but most run on blockchains like:
->Ethereum
->Tron
->BSC
 which have trade-offs: high fees, congestion or security risks
If(When) stablecoins moved to a Plasma, these processes could(will) improve

Ultra Cheap Transfers
Plasma makes txs cost just fractions of a cent

That means even the smallest payments (like buying bread or paying $1 to a worker) become possible, no more $5-30 gas fees for simple tx

Massive Scale (billions of tx/day)
Plasma can process way more txs than today’s chains(Ethereum wont be used for payments never again)

Remittances, payroll and merchant payments could all happen instantly, even if billions of people use it daily

Instant Finality
Settlements are secured by Bitcoin, so they cant be reversed or tampered with
Families, workers,regular users that just want to send their money and businesses trust payments like real cash

Bank-Free Inclusion
People in countries with weak banks (Nigeria, Argentina,Lebanon,Venezuela.... ) could store, send and spend stablecoins directly without middlemen

Micro-subscriptions also become possible with Plasma (Netflix per hour, Uber per ride) because fees dont eat the whole payment

Plasma could turn stablecoins from a crypto trading tool into the backbone of global money, making it:
->easy 
->cheap
->safe
for anyone, anywhere to use them like cash

👉Basically: today stablecoins work for some people, some of the tim
🔥With Plasma, they could work for everyone, all the time

I already got a interesting plan what I want to do in few years after Plasma's mainnet launch

I wanna buy a real estate in Dubai and make a payment in stablecoins via @PlasmaFDN 
Lets check the process in details👇
1⃣Most property developers and brokers in Dubai accept USDT and USDC, I would choose USDT ofc

2⃣Find a Crypto-Friendly Real Estate Developer or Broker
Several major developers (like DAMAC, Emaar and Select Group) and agencies already allow crypto payments
Work with a licensed real estate broker who has explicit support for crypto txs

3⃣Then I would choose property I want

4⃣PAYMENT, the most interesting part
You ll typically sign a Memorandum of Understanding with the seller

The agreed price will be converted into a stablecoin equivalent at the market rate

Payment happens via a crypto payment processor or directly to the developer’s designated crypto wallet and in few years I believe that we will be able to do that via Plasma(Im sure that it will be possible)

Plasma has everything that developers for real estate would wish
->Fast
->Secured by Bitcoin
->Almost NO fees

FUTURE WITH PLASMA IS HUGE

TRILLIONS🕊️

The streets of #NewDelhi echoed today with the voices of Tibetan exiles and supporters, as hundreds gathered to protest the visit of Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi for the 24th round of border talks with India. What Beijing hoped would be a quiet diplomatic engagement was met instead with a fierce reminder that Tibet’s struggle for freedom cannot be silenced.

Carrying the Tibetan national flag (banned in occupied Tibet but defiantly raised here), protesters condemned Wang Yi as the face of Beijing’s lies, repression, and colonial rule. Placards read “Free Tibet”, “China Out of Tibet”, and “Wang Yi Go Back”, turning the capital into a stage of resistance against Chinese authoritarianism.

Tibetans shouted slogans denouncing China’s occupation of Tibet since 1950, Beijing’s destruction of monasteries, mass surveillance, and forced boarding schools that tear Tibetan children from their culture. Many drew direct parallels between China’s ongoing border aggression against India and its decades-long military occupation of Tibet, calling both part of the same imperial expansion project.

“𝐖𝐚𝐧𝐠 𝐘𝐢 𝐫𝐞𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐚 𝐫𝐞𝐠𝐢𝐦𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐡𝐚𝐬 𝐤𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐝, 𝐣𝐚𝐢𝐥𝐞𝐝, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐬𝐢𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐝 𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐩𝐞𝐨𝐩𝐥𝐞 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐬𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐲 𝐲𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐬. 𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐚 𝐦𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝐧𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝐁𝐞𝐢𝐣𝐢𝐧𝐠’𝐬 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐦𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐬. 𝐂𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐚 𝐡𝐚𝐬 𝐧𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐤𝐞𝐩𝐭 𝐚 𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐥𝐞 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐦𝐢𝐬𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐓𝐢𝐛𝐞𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐬, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐢𝐭 𝐰𝐨𝐧’𝐭 𝐤𝐞𝐞𝐩 𝐚𝐧𝐲 𝐭𝐨 𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐚 𝐞𝐢𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫,” 
𝐬𝐚𝐢𝐝 𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐓𝐢𝐛𝐞𝐭𝐚𝐧 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐡 𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐚𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐭𝐞𝐬𝐭.

𝐀 𝐏𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝 𝐊𝐧𝐨𝐰𝐬 𝐓𝐨𝐨 𝐖𝐞𝐥𝐥

China’s duplicity with Tibet is not an isolated case. Around the globe, nations are waking up to the cost of Beijing’s broken promises:

🔴#Philippines recently stood its ground in the South China Sea, successfully pushing back Chinese ships in contested waters. Manila has learned the hard way that Beijing’s “peaceful rise” masks coercion and bullying.

🔴#Italy is now moving to curb Chinese stakes in strategic companies, fearing infiltration into sensitive sectors like infrastructure and high-tech manufacturing.

🔴#EuropeanUnion has slapped restrictions on Chinese banks and investments, wary of Beijing’s growing economic leverage.

🔴#UnitedStates continues to warn allies of the dangers of overdependence on Chinese technology, blocking Beijing-linked companies from sensitive sectors.

🔴#Japan and #Australia have both tightened security ties with India and the U.S., directly citing China’s aggression as the driving force.

What unites these actions is a growing recognition that China cannot be taken at its word. The “peace” it sells is merely a pause before the next expansion.

𝐓𝐢𝐛𝐞𝐭 𝐚𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐭 𝐨𝐟 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐭

The timing of Wang Yi’s visit could not be more controversial. While China’s state media paints the border talks as a step toward “stability,” India’s security forces remain locked in tense standoffs with Chinese troops along the Line of Actual Control (#LAC). Tibetans argue that the root of the conflict lies in China’s illegal annexation of Tibet, which once served as a peaceful buffer between the two #Asian giants.

International human rights groups have also warned that Tibet is facing one of the world’s most severe crackdowns. Freedom House rates Tibet as the least free place on earth, alongside Syria. More than 160 Tibetans have self-immolated since 2009 in desperate protest against #Chineserepression, acts of sacrifice largely ignored by global powers wary of offending Beijing.
